top_story: The 30 September bombing of a school in Minab that killed 120 children deepened Iranian public trauma just as pressure on Tehran intensified, sharpening the domestic stakes of confrontation with Washington. By 5 October, mounting tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz pointed to a calibrated Iranian response to sanctions and currency stress, using maritime pressure to raise the economic cost of coercion without moving immediately to open war. That same day, U.S. intelligence assessments described Israel as vulnerable to civil conflict ahead of the 27 October elections, with disputes over conscription, settler violence, and the condition of returning soldiers exposing severe internal strain. The regional picture is one of parallel escalation and fragmentation, where external military pressure and internal social fracture are reinforcing instability across two central U.S. partners and adversaries alike.
